transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

For months I’ve felt unusually ‘up’ and on edge all the time, like my mood is cranked way higher than normal and I can’t dial it back. It's gotten to the point where it's really starting to impact my work and my home life, which is why I'm here.

Have these unusually high, on-edge moods ever started during or soon after using alcohol, recreational drugs, or stimulant medications like Adderall or cocaine? Or do they happen even when you haven’t used any substances?
No, I don't use recreational drugs, stimulants, or heavy alcohol at all. These moods happen entirely on their own, without any kind of substance triggering them.

Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt very depressed or lost interest in most things most of the day, nearly every day? If so, did that happen before or between these high-energy periods?

No, I haven't really experienced periods of feeling deeply depressed or losing interest in things like that. My struggle has really just been this constant, extreme 'up' and wired feeling that I can't seem to shut down.

During these high-energy periods, have you ever had hallucinations or strongly believed things that others said were not true, like having special powers or being watched? If yes, did that only happen when your mood was extremely high?

I haven't had hallucinations or felt like I was being watched, but I have been absolutely convinced that I'm on the verge of a major, field-changing breakthrough that only I can see. I've felt like I'm operating on a completely different intellectual level than my colleagues, but this extreme self-confidence only happens when I'm in these high-energy, "up" periods.

When you felt you were on the verge of a field-changing breakthrough, did other people see that belief as clearly unrealistic or out of touch with reality? Also, have you had any other experiences during these times, like hearing or seeing things others didn’t?

Yes, my colleagues and department leadership definitely questioned my plans and saw them as completely unrealistic, which was incredibly frustrating because I felt I was operating on a totally different level than they were. But as for hearing or seeing things that others didn't, no, I've never had any unusual sensory experiences like that.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a sustained abnormally elevated/activated mood for months with significant impairment in work and home life, no substance trigger, and mood-congruent grandiose delusional beliefs judged unrealistic by others. There is no history of major depressive episodes provided. This is most consistent with a manic episode with psychotic symptoms.
